clips.titel: Psychologist Alison Gopnik on why AI is no match for a 4-year-old
clips.wortlaut: And I think that picture, the picture of a system that develops, that changes over time, and in particular, as we'll see, a system that's cared for by, uh, by humans or cared for by other intelligent agents, that's the secret of human intelligence.
clips.kontext_davor: It's an absolutely beautiful story that I highly recommend. (Ted Chiang, 'The Life Cycle of Software Objects': Menschen adoptieren KI-Babys, ziehen sie gross und lassen sie gehen.)
clips.kontext_danach: And that's the kind of system you'd need if you wanted a system that had the same kind of intelligence as humans.

clips.titel: Are we betting too much on AI? | Nobel Laureate Daron Acemoglu
clips.wortlaut: The direction of AI is going to be whatever the leading companies decide. But we have huge influence on these companies, which so far we have not exercised.
clips.kontext_davor: There isn't a single direction of AI. We have to shape that direction, and the way we do that is via our institutions, via the democratic process, and of course, we need to ensure that the firms, the companies that are at the forefront of AI, get on board. They will have an influence on this. It's not like a bureaucrat sitting in the White House or somewhere in Ottawa can decide what the direction of AI is going to be.
clips.kontext_danach: (Sinead Bovell:) And so what is your thesis for pro-worker AI? How does that actually work in practice?
